title: Pennsylvania governor issues order on data center development
key_facts: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro signed an executive order on 18 Aug 2026 to give municipalities more control and set stricter guardrails for data centers; governors in Maryland and Virginia have since followed.

Developers who sign a binding agreement with the Department of Environmental Protection to meet the GRID standards can submit permit applications immediately, but permits are not issued until municipalities approve.
Developers who do not sign face no DEP review until local approval is secured and lose the tax exemption on data center computer equipment.
The order removes data centers from the PA Permit Fast Track Program, bans nondisclosure agreements and requires annual energy and water reporting from July 2027.
A Quinnipiac poll in July found 74% of Pennsylvania voters opposed to a local AI data center; proposals exist for over 100 more.
As of 18 Sep, a Shapiro administration official said no developers had signed on.
More than a dozen bills are pending; NRDC says binding rules need legislation.
quote_evidence: As of September 18, one month after the executive order was signed, a Shapiro administration official told the Bay Journal thatno data center developers had signed on.
The upcoming November gubernatorial election is a reminder that executive orders come and go with administrations.
“If we want binding requirements on data center projects, [GRID] has to have the full force of law behind it, which requires legislation.”
why_it_matters_hint: Shows states shifting power to towns, with the first test of whether developers sign up.
notes: Older event (18 Aug 2026); this 8 Oct article adds the no-signers update.
